rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for the pop-music genre.

example.english: This pop music is great for dancing.
example.traditional: 呢首流行音樂好啱跳舞。
example.jyutping: ni1 sau2 lau4 hang4 jam1 ngok6 hou2 ngaam1 tiu3 mou5

rows.note: Use 擺 as the all-purpose verb for putting something somewhere, with the quickness supplied by context.

example.english: I'll pop the book on the table first.
example.jyutping: ngo5 baai2 bun2 syu1 hai2 toi4 min6 sin1

rows.note: Use 彈出嚟 when something suddenly springs or comes out, especially from a confined place.

example.english: I saw the little ball pop out suddenly.
example.traditional: 我見到個波仔突然彈出嚟。
example.jyutping: ngo5 gin3 dou2 go3 bo1 zai2 dat6 jin4 taan4 ceot1 lei4

rows.note: Use this for the father reading of “pop”; Cantonese normally uses a separate word for grandfather.

example.english: My pop cooks for me all the time.
example.traditional: 我爸爸成日煮飯畀我食。
example.jyutping: ngo5 baa4 baa4 seng4 jat6 zyu2 faan6 bei2 ngo5 sik6

rows.note: Use this for the grandfather reading, specifically a paternal grandfather.

example.english: My pop used to live in the countryside.
example.jyutping: ngo5 je4 je2 ji5 cin4 zyu6 hai2 hoeng1 haa6

rows.note: Use 打開 for popping open a lid, cover, or hood; the suddenness is supplied by context.

example.english: You just press it and the box lid will pop open.
example.traditional: 你一撳個盒蓋就打開喇。
example.jyutping: nei5 jat1 gam6 go3 hap6 goi3 zau6 daa2 hoi1 laa3

rows.note: Use this for a distinctive feature or visual accent that makes something stand out.

example.english: This mural is the café’s pop, the feature that makes it stand out.
example.traditional: 呢幅壁畫係間咖啡店嘅亮點。
example.jyutping: ni1 fuk1 bik1 waa2 hai6 gaan1 gaa3 fe1 dim3 ge3 loeng6 dim2

rows.note: Use 整爆 when deliberately causing something such as a balloon to burst.

example.english: They used a needle to pop the balloon.
example.jyutping: keoi5 jung6 zam1 zing2 baau3 go3 hei3 kau4
